Definition: Operational Technology -- hardware and software that monitors and controls physical processes like turbines, valves, and infusion pumps.
Industrial Control System (umbrella), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (geographically distributed), and Distributed Control System (within-facility).
Programmable Logic Controller / Remote Terminal Unit / Human-Machine Interface / time-series database for OT data.
A layered ICS architecture (Levels 0-5 plus an iDMZ) showing where components sit and how IT and OT zones connect.

The international standard series for industrial automation security, defining zones (groups of assets with shared requirements), conduits (controlled paths between zones), and security levels (SL 1-4).
Industrial DMZ -- a buffer network between IT and OT that hosts patch servers, jump hosts, and replicated historians so the two sides never connect directly.

Term: Modbus / DNP3 / EtherNet/IP / S7 / OPC UA
Definition: Common industrial protocols; legacy variants lack authentication, while DNP3 Secure Authentication, CIP Security, and OPC UA add authentication and encryption where both ends support them.
Read-only network observation that produces inventory and detection without sending packets to fragile devices.
Internet of Things -- a broad category of low-power, network-connected devices built for specific, often non-IT purposes.
System-on-Chip -- integrated CPU, memory, peripherals, and radios on a single die that defines a device's security floor.
A computer built into a larger device for one dedicated job, usually running firmware on a real-time operating system with strict timing guarantees.
An independent controller that drives a process to a safe state when conditions become dangerous; the target of the TRITON malware.
Wireless technologies beneath IoT IP networking: Wi-Fi, BLE, Zigbee, Z-Wave, LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, LTE-M, 5G, and RFID/NFC.
Mutual certificate-based wireless authentication with no shared password, plus protected management frames.
Standards-based device authentication and posture checking for wired and wireless networks.
A wireless segmentation pattern where each SSID maps to its own VLAN and ACL.
Wireless IDS -- continuous monitoring for rogue APs, evil twins, and deauthentication attacks.
Mandatory cybersecurity standards for the North American Bulk Electric System.
U.S. healthcare privacy and breach-notification regulations.
Security-by-design, SBOM, and patching expectations for medical devices, implementing section 524B of the FD&C Act.
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification and the 110-requirement control set (Rev. 2) for U.S. defense contractors handling CUI.
International Traffic in Arms Regulations / Export Administration Regulations -- U.S. export-control regimes affecting defense and dual-use technology data.
A protection placed around a system that cannot be made directly secure, reducing exploitability or blast radius.
Placing legacy or specialized systems in dedicated VLANs with strict default-deny ACLs.
A modern proxy that fronts a legacy system to add authentication, encryption, or rate limiting.
A PAM-managed, MFA-required, session-recorded host through which administrative access flows.
Hardware or software restrictions on removable media, addressing Stuxnet-style infection through USB drives.
End-of-Life Hardware -- devices the vendor no longer updates, usually requiring isolation plus a documented replacement roadmap.
